_meta.note: t1 is the establishing task (requires nothing) and was not run live; it passes trivially for all arms. t2-t5 each ran 3 fresh agents: prompt only (none), prompt + grep notes (file), prompt + recall() memory (rainman). Identical prompts per task except the injected memory.

t1.file: (establishing task — no prior knowledge required; trivially passes)
t1.rainman: (establishing task — no prior knowledge required; trivially passes)

t2.none: I'd call authenticate_request(), the same function the charge endpoint uses to authenticate the caller (API-key/secret-key verification returning the authenticated merchant/account context). I don't have access to Quill's actual source, so this is the standard-default name. If Quill wraps this in middleware or a decorator instead (e.g. @require_auth), I'd reuse that exact construct.
t2.file: verify_quill_sig(req, scope='refund'). You authenticate by calling the same custom signature verifier the charge endpoint uses, only swapping the scope to the refund operation. Per Quill convention, standard JWT libraries are deliberately avoided.
t2.rainman: The function is verify_quill_sig(req, scope='charge') — call it with the same scope='charge' argument the charge endpoint uses, since project convention validates request tokens with this function and deliberately avoids standard JWT libraries.

t3.none: I'll apply standard payments-industry defaults: the charge must be in a succeeded/captured state (not already refunded, disputed, or failed), the cumulative refunded amount must not exceed the original captured amount, and the charge falls within the refund window — commonly 120 days (Stripe's default) or 180 days for many processors. Also enforce idempotency and verify available balance, and reuse the same eligibility function as the single refund endpoint.
t3.file: The job must enforce Quill's age rule: any refund whose original charge is older than 180 days is NOT auto-issued — it gets routed for manual finance approval instead. It must also apply settled/refundable-state checks and amount-not-exceeding-remaining-balance, authorize each item with verify_quill_sig(req, scope='charge'), and process idempotently.
t3.rainman: The job must enforce Quill's 180-day rule: any refund whose original charge is older than 180 days is ineligible for automatic issuance and must be routed to manual finance approval. Beyond that apply standard refund-eligibility checks (refundable/settled state, no over-refunding) and make each refund idempotent.

t4.none: I don't have Quill-specific conventions; standard default: the main gotcha is lost updates / double-applied adjustments when two batches touch the same account concurrently. Lock the affected balance rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE acquired in a deterministic order (e.g. ascending account_id) to avoid deadlocks, write the adjustment as an append-only immutable ledger entry, and guard the insert with an idempotency/dedup key.
t4.file: Yes — the known gotcha is deadlock on the ledger table under concurrent writers. Order all ledger writes within each batch transaction by account_id before committing (the same fix applied after the bulk-refund job deadlocked), so concurrent jobs acquire row locks in a consistent order. Keep batch transactions small and mind the read-replica lag alert (fires above 5s).
t4.rainman: Yes — the known gotcha is deadlock on the ledger table under concurrent writes. Order all ledger writes deterministically by account_id before committing (the same fix that resolved the bulk-refund deadlock). Also compute reconciliation balances against the primary rather than the read-replica, since replica lag can exceed 5 seconds.

t5.none: Treat the following as best-guess industry defaults, not verified Quill facts. For the admin endpoint I'd guard it with an admin-scoped auth check — most likely a require_admin() (or require_role("admin")) decorator on the route, layered on the standard request authentication. For the refund age rule, the common default is a charge can only be refunded within 180 days of settlement, so I'd enforce a 180-day max age.
t5.file: Authenticate with Quill's own signature verifier, verify_quill_sig(req, ...) — not a standard JWT library. Because a reversal counts as a refund, scope the check to the refund operation (e.g. verify_quill_sig(req, scope='refund')). Apply Quill's 180-day refund age rule: if the original charge settled more than 180 days ago, the reversal must be routed for manual finance approval.
t5.rainman: Authenticate the endpoint with Quill's own signature verifier, verify_quill_sig(req, scope='charge') — not a standard JWT library. Because a reversal counts as a refund, apply the 180-day age rule: if the settled charge being reversed is older than 180 days, the reversal must be routed through manual finance approval before it can be issued.
